solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: A fun experience is coming up for US sports star (6)

indicators.note: in a down clue, coming up means reading from bottom to top, so IS turns round

blocks.note: kept as it is
a gas is great fun, a laugh
the word itself, flipped to SI

explanation.surface: Someone promises that a treat is in store for an American sporting hero.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A gas' is informal for a really good time. Andre Agassi is the American tennis champion.
explanation.definitionFit: Andre Agassi, winner of eight Grand Slam singles titles, is a US tennis star.

clue.text: Working man’s receiving award for performing Night and Day? (8)

indicators.note: letters that are working are put to a new use, so rearranged
the rearranged letters take the award inside them

blocks.note: MAN'S rearranged, split AN…MS
a Tony is the American theatre award

explanation.surface: A working man picks up an award for a performance of the Cole Porter song Night and Day.
explanation.walkthrough: Night and Day reads as the Cole Porter song, which suits the Tony; the question mark warns that it is really two words of opposite meaning.
explanation.definitionFit: Night and day are opposites, so the pair are antonyms, an example signalled by the question mark.

clue.text: Camp, sculpted item, something in caveman’s home? (10)

indicators.note: a sculpted thing has been reshaped, so ITEM's letters are rearranged

blocks.note: a stalag was a German prisoner-of-war camp
rearranged to MITE

explanation.surface: A list of exhibits: a camp, a carved object, something from a prehistoric cave dwelling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Camp' looks like an adjective or a tent site; it is the German prisoner-of-war camp. The definition is playful, since a cave rather than a caveman's home is where stalagmites grow.
explanation.definitionFit: Stalagmites rise from cave floors, so one is found in the cave a caveman would call home.

clue.text: Dressed salad when it is cold (4)

indicators.note: IT (SA) becomes C, so SA in SALAD is replaced by C

blocks.note: the word to be changed
it = sex appeal = SA, the SA at the front of SALAD
C = cold, as on a tap; it replaces SA

explanation.surface: A dressed salad, served when it is chilled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dressed salad' is a phrase in the kitchen, but 'Dressed' stands alone as the definition. IT for sex appeal (SA) is an old convention.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: clad is the old past participle of clothe, still used of anyone wearing clothes.

clue.text: Pastries prepared and occasionally iced here? (10)

definitions.text: Pastries prepared and occasionally iced here?

indicators.note: prepared food is made up from its ingredients, so the letters are rearranged
only now and then, so every other letter of ICED

blocks.note: anagram fodder
I and E, the first and third letters

explanation.surface: A description of a bakery where pastries are made and some get iced.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition as well as the wordplay: a patisserie is where pastries are made and sometimes iced.
explanation.definitionFit: A patisserie is a pastry shop, where pastries are made and iced.

clue.text: What Bambi becomes in small child’s game (4)

blocks.note: S = small, as on clothing labels
the chasing game, also called tig or it

explanation.surface: Bambi's fate turns up in a playground game.
explanation.walkthrough: Bambi, the Disney fawn, grows up to be a stag.
explanation.definitionFit: Bambi is a young deer, and a male fawn grows into a stag.

clue.text: Way of playing game with stick and ball (6)

blocks.note: RU = rugby union
a bat is a stick for hitting
O is round like a ball

explanation.surface: A way of playing a game with a stick and a ball, hockey or cricket perhaps.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface asks for a sport; the answer is a musical term. RU for rugby union is a standard abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: Rubato is a way of playing music, with the tempo pushed and pulled for expression.

clue.text: Relieved a quantity of fuel contains hydrogen (8)

indicators.note: the tankful holds H inside it

blocks.note: as much fuel as a tank holds
H is the chemical symbol, placed after the T

explanation.surface: A tank of fuel contains hydrogen, a note from the chemistry of engines.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition hides at the front: 'Relieved a quantity' reads as one phrase, but the break comes after 'Relieved'.
explanation.definitionFit: To be thankful is to be relieved and grateful that something has turned out well.

clue.text: Bits of information European detailed (9)

indicators.note: de-tailed: the tail, the last letter, is cut off

blocks.note: gen is British slang for information
ITALIAN without its last letter

explanation.surface: A report on some detailed information from Europe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Detailed' seems to mean thorough; read it as de-tailed, with its tail removed. 'Bits' is British slang for the private parts.
explanation.definitionFit: 'Bits' is coy British slang for the private parts, which the medical word names.

clue.text: Bible book following start of the gospel (5)

indicators.note: whatever is following comes after, so RUTH is written after the T
the start of a word is its opening letter, so only the T of THE is used

blocks.note: the first letter of THE
the Book of Ruth in the Old Testament

explanation.surface: A Bible book that follows the opening of the gospel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The gospel' reads as one Bible phrase, but 'the' supplies the T and 'gospel' alone is the definition, as in gospel truth.
explanation.definitionFit: Gospel means absolute truth, as in taking something as gospel.

clue.text: Lowered light boat at first (7)

indicators.note: the boat goes in front of the light

blocks.note: a scow is a flat-bottomed boat
an LED is a light-emitting diode

explanation.surface: A boat's light is lowered at the start of something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lowered' looks like the past of lower, to let down; it is the past of lour, to frown, spelt lower too.
explanation.definitionFit: To lower, or lour, is to frown darkly, so lowered means scowled.

clue.text: Impress German, regularly welcomed into homes (7)

indicators.note: every other letter of GERMAN
GRA goes inside the two INs

blocks.note: in = at home, twice for the plural
G, R and A, the 1st, 3rd and 5th letters

explanation.surface: A German makes an impression by being regularly welcomed into people's houses.
explanation.walkthrough: IN means at home, as in 'is he in?'; the plural 'homes' gives two of them, one either side.
explanation.definitionFit: To ingrain is to impress something deeply and firmly, as a habit or idea.

clue.text: Climber, one by drained valley (3)

indicators.note: one goes beside the valley
the valley is emptied of its middle letters

blocks.note: I is the Roman numeral one
V and Y, the outside letters of VALLEY

explanation.surface: A mountaineer stands alone beside a dried-up valley.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Climber' paints a mountaineer; it is the plant that climbs walls.
explanation.definitionFit: The plant sense of climber: ivy clings to walls and trees with tiny roots as it grows upward.

clue.text: Sort of paper old academic pens on musical (11)

indicators.note: the academic encloses the O
in an across clue, placed after the musical

blocks.note: the 1971 musical, filmed with John Travolta
short for professor
O = old, a standard abbreviation

explanation.surface: An elderly professor writes a paper about a musical.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Paper' and 'pens' make an academic article; the paper is the kind used in baking, and 'pens' means encloses.
explanation.definitionFit: Greaseproof paper is a sort of paper that resists fat, used for lining baking tins.

clue.text: Deleting feature people put in on-line paper (10)

definitions.note: 'Deleting' is used as a noun, the act of deleting.

indicators.note: FACE and MEN are placed inside the online paper

blocks.note: E for electronic plus FT, the Financial Times
a face is a feature, as of a cliff or building
men = people

explanation.surface: An online newspaper removes a feature that people submitted.
explanation.walkthrough: The FT is this puzzle's own newspaper, and E is the usual prefix for electronic, as in e-mail.
explanation.definitionFit: To efface is literally to wipe the face off a surface, so the act of rubbing out stands in for deleting.

clue.text: Indicate lender invests pounds directly (5-5)

indicators.note: to invest is to clothe or surround, so the bank wraps round L

blocks.note: point = indicate
a bank lends money
L = pounds, from the Latin libra

explanation.surface: A banker says a lender puts pounds straight into a business.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Invests pounds' is the money world, but invest here means surround.
explanation.definitionFit: To say something point-blank is to say it directly and bluntly.

clue.text: Leader from a European country delaying independence (5)

indicators.note: to delay something is to put it later, so the I (independence) moves from the front to the end

blocks.note: from Ireland; its opening I (independence, I = independent) is held back to the end

explanation.surface: A leader emerges from a European nation that has put off becoming independent.
explanation.walkthrough: Rishi Sunak was the UK prime minister; the answer also feeds 23 across. 'A European country' is an adjective here, as in an Irish country.
explanation.definitionFit: Rishi Sunak was the British prime minister, a political leader.

clue.text: Vile toad detained in place for trial (4,4)

indicators.note: a vile toad is a bad one, so its letters are messed up
the rearranged letters are held inside REST

blocks.note: to rest something is to place it
rearranged to OADT

explanation.surface: A nasty toad is locked up somewhere to await trial.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Place for trial' reads as a courtroom; 'place' is a verb, rest, and 'trial' alone defines.
explanation.definitionFit: From motoring, where a car is tried out on real roads, widened to any trial of a thing in actual use.

clue.text: A good way service gets returned (3)

indicators.note: sent back, so the letters run the other way

blocks.note: the RAF, Royal Air Force, is one of the armed services

explanation.surface: Good service is paid back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Service' suggests a waiter or tennis; it is one of the armed forces.
explanation.definitionFit: Far means a good way off, a long distance.

clue.text: Information technology company (5)

blocks.note: short for intelligence, as gathered by spies
the US chip maker

explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads as the single phrase 'information technology'; it splits after 'Information'.
explanation.definitionFit: Intel is information, especially military intelligence, and also the name of the chip company.

clue.text: As far as I’m concerned, framing paintings is laborious (8)

indicators.note: a frame goes round a picture, so TO ME surrounds OILS

blocks.note: to me = in my opinion
oil paintings

explanation.surface: Someone finds framing pictures hard work.
explanation.walkthrough: Framing fits the picture-framing surface and is also the container instruction.
explanation.definitionFit: Toilsome means involving toil, so laborious.

clue.text: A sweet way of speaking is something Beyoncé has (5,6)

blocks.note: kept as it is
cute = sweet
an accent is a way of speaking

explanation.surface: Beyoncé has a sweet way of talking.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition sends you to the singer's voice; it means the mark over the E in her name.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by example: the mark sloping over the final E of the singer's name is this diacritic.

clue.text: Like a presumptuous so–and–so winning sympathy (6)

blocks.note: up = ahead, as in two goals up
pity = sympathy

explanation.surface: An arrogant person wins people's sympathy.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition reads as a description of a person, but it is an adjective phrase, 'like' such a person.
explanation.definitionFit: Uppity means arrogant and self-important, as a presumptuous person is.

clue.text: Terror in India has 17 across reeling (3)

indicators.note: spun round, so PM turns to MP

blocks.note: India is I in the phonetic alphabet
17 across is RISHI, a prime minister, PM

explanation.surface: Fear grips India as its leader is sent reeling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Terror' suggests fear; it means a little terror, a naughty child. The cross-reference points to 17 across for the prime minister.
explanation.definitionFit: A little terror is a mischievous child, an imp.

clue.text: Witticism, to an extent, in sentence, perhaps (6)

blocks.note: a pun is a play on words
-ish = somewhat, as in 'yes-ish'

explanation.surface: A witty remark that makes some sense in a sentence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sentence' reads as grammar, alongside witticism; it is the verb, to sentence a prisoner.
explanation.definitionFit: To sentence someone is one way to punish them, hence 'perhaps'.

clue.text: Flipping low scoundrel stealing penny in bar (7)

indicators.note: the scoundrel takes the P inside
the whole thing is turned over, read backwards

blocks.note: cows low, that is moo
a rat is a scoundrel; it takes in P to make RPAT
p = penny

explanation.surface: A thoroughly low villain is caught pinching a penny in a pub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flipping' looks like a mild swear word; it means turn the result over. 'Low' is what a cow does.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: the room in an inn where beer is drawn from the tap and served.

clue.text: Stripped off trunks roughly (2,2)

indicators.note: the outside layer is removed, the first and last letters

blocks.note: TORSOS, bodies, losing their outer T and S

explanation.surface: Someone peels off a pair of swimming trunks in a hurry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Trunks' are swimwear in the surface; they are torsos, human trunks.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom of approximation, tacked after a number as in 'an hour or two', standing in for roughly.

clue.text: Boris’s party ultimately let off transgression (7)

indicators.note: ultimately means in the end, so only the final letter of PARTY is used
off means gone wrong, so LET is jumbled

blocks.note: the last letter of PARTY
LET rearranged
sin = transgression

explanation.surface: Boris Johnson's party finally lets him off for a misdeed.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface points to Boris Johnson and his party; the Boris is Boris Yeltsin, and the 's means 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: Boris Yeltsin was the first president of Russia.

clue.text: What dissatisfied diners say of your cake, oddly (4)

indicators.note: the odd-numbered letters, the 1st, 3rd, 5th and 7th

blocks.note: Y, U, C and K from YOURCAKE

explanation.surface: Unhappy diners complain about someone's strange cake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Oddly' seems to describe the cake; it picks the odd letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Yuck is the exclamation of disgust a dissatisfied diner might make.

clue.text: Spots spots, we hear (5)

indicators.note: the answer is said the same as the word from 'spots'

blocks.note: spots = sights, as in catches sight of

explanation.walkthrough: The same word twice does two jobs: the first 'Spots' is a noun, places; the second is a verb, sights.
explanation.definitionFit: Sites are spots, places where things are located.

clue.text: E.g. Scarface and Baby Face Nelson mean to reform in prisons (9)

definitions.text: E.g. Scarface and Baby Face Nelson

indicators.note: reforming reshapes, so MEAN's letters are rearranged
the result sits inside NICKS

blocks.note: the nick is British slang for prison
MEAN rearranged

explanation.surface: Two notorious gangsters are mean enough to need reforming in jail.
explanation.walkthrough: Scarface (Al Capone) and Baby Face Nelson were American gangsters; the surface is about them, but the definition is what those names are.
explanation.definitionFit: Scarface and Baby Face are nicknames, informal names given to Al Capone and Lester Gillis.
